summary: Closure verification of dry-run #1 highs is partial: REV-L2-001 (buyerEmail) is closed by construction (Checkout step 2 reads identity.profile.read, forwards profile.Email as BuyerEmail, Order requires it as binding:'required,email'); REV-L2-002 (env-var unification on INTERNAL_SHARED_SECRET) is closed by construction (all 4 recipient services read the same name; Payment migrated from INTERNAL_SECRET); REV-L2-003 (constant-time compare) is closed by construction (order, inventory, payment all use crypto/subtle.ConstantTimeCompare; no plain ==/!= secret comparisons survive). REV-L2-004 (compound stub dead-end) is ONLY HALF closed: order.cancel-on-checkout-failure is a real handler now, but Order's onPaymentFailed / onPaymentExpired / onReservationExpired consumers are still TODO stubs (consumer.go:139-156) — every payment failure or reservation expiry leaves the order frozen in PENDING_PAYMENT forever, breaking the saga at the system level. Beyond closure, four high cross-component bugs that single-component Reviewer-L1 reviewers could not see by construction: (1) Checkout generates orderID (UUID v7) and uses it as the key for inventory.reservation, payment.intent, and the Idempotency-Key, but Order's CreateFromCheckoutRequest has no orderId field at all — Order generates its own uuid.New() and ignores Checkout's value, so the order row id and the reservation/payment-intent foreign keys diverge; payment.completed events keyed by Checkout's orderID will not find a matching orders row at Order's consumer (GetByIDForUpdate returns nil, transition silently skipped) — every successful checkout commit produces a stuck order; (2) the shared common/middleware/auth.go used by 7 backends never validates tokenType claim, so a refresh JWT (14d TTL) authenticates against every Bearer-protected route across the platform — system-wide JWT type-confusion; (3) Idempotency-Key carriage protocol is heterogeneous across the 8 components — frontend originates as HTTP header, the Next.js [...path] catch-all does not forward it (no dedicated /api/checkout/commit route), Checkout reads it as header, Order/Inventory accept it as JSON-body field (under idempotencyKey), Payment expects it as header but the Checkout client never sends one — the chain breaks at every hop except inventory; (4) Order writes events.order.cancelled to outbox_events on cancel-on-checkout-failure but no outbox publisher goroutine is wired in main.go — every cancel orphans the inventory reservation forever (per-component finding REV-ORDER-004 escalates to system-level when seen against Inventory's state-driven consumer that will never receive the event). Sole-writer rule on orders.status verified: a grep across all 7 backends finds no UPDATE orders SET status outside backend/services/order/app/order/access/storage_order.go::UpdateStatus — invariant intact. Cookie-attribute parity (Set-Cookie at issuance vs clearance) is broken in frontend lib/auth.ts:59,63 (clear strings omit SameSite + Secure attributes) — REV-FRONTEND-WEB-002 already filed at L1 and applies at every Set-Cookie clear site (refresh, logout, withAuth) so the cross-component impact is real but already escalated. The verdict is block: REV-L2-004 partial closure plus four new cross-component highs gates the merge.

findings.description: Checkout generates orderID via uuid.NewV7() at handler_commit.go:336 and uses that string as (a) the inventory.reservation.create key (line 371), (b) the payment.intent.create key (line 438), (c) the Idempotency-Key on the order.create-from-checkout body (line 410), AND (d) the orderId field passed to Order in client_order.go:53. However Order's CreateFromCheckoutRequest DTO (domain.go:124-136) has no orderId field — only idempotencyKey, customerUserId, buyerEmail, addressSnapshot, items, subtotal, shippingFee, couponDiscount, grandTotal. handler_create_from_checkout.go:42 generates its own orderID := uuid.New().String() and persists THAT as orders.id, ignoring the value Checkout sent. Net effect at runtime: orders.id (UUID v4 from Order) ≠ inventory.reservations.order_id (UUID v7 from Checkout) ≠ payment_intents.order_id (UUID v7 from Checkout). When payment.completed flows back via Kafka (orderId = UUID v7 from Payment's view), Order's onPaymentCompleted handler calls GetByIDForUpdate(UUID v7) which returns nil; consumer.go:88-91 logs 'unknown orderId, skipping' and commits a no-op. Every successful checkout commit therefore produces an order permanently frozen in PENDING_PAYMENT — the customer is charged (Payment state=PAID) but the customer-visible order detail page reads PENDING_PAYMENT forever. This is the cross-component escalation of per-component REV-ORDER-001 (Order generates own UUID); R-L1 saw it as a local idempotency miss; the L2 view shows a four-table cross-database key-divergence with a paid-but-not-paid-to-the-customer end state.
findings.recommendation: Two coordinated changes. (1) Tech-Lead: amend contracts.json#order.create-from-checkout request schema to include orderId:string (UUID, required) and clarify in contract notes that Checkout owns orderID generation; orders.id MUST equal request.orderId; idempotencyKey MUST equal request.orderId. (2) Order Dev: add OrderID string `json:"orderId" binding:"required,uuid"` to CreateFromCheckoutRequest in domain.go:126; replace handler_create_from_checkout.go:42 `orderID := uuid.New().String()` with `orderID := req.OrderID` (after the binding validation already runs); on Postgres unique_violation 23505 on orders_pk inside Insert, SELECT the existing row by id and return 200 with the cached envelope (closing REV-ORDER-002 in the same diff). End-to-end test: a Checkout retry with the same Idempotency-Key produces the SAME orderId on every reply and the inventory/payment/order rows all share it.

findings.description: backend/common/middleware/auth.go is the canonical Bearer-JWT middleware reused by every protected route across SEVEN backends (checkout, order, identity, payment, inventory, cart, catalog — confirmed via `grep middleware.JWT` across services/). It performs signature verify, parse, and ValidateClaims, but never inspects claims.Extra['tokenType']. Identity mints both ACCESS (15min TTL, tokenType='access') and REFRESH (14d TTL, tokenType='refresh') JWTs from the SAME ES256 keypair (identity/router/deps.go AccessSigner/RefreshSigner share cfg.JWT.PrivateKeyPEM); cross-cutting.auth.claims declares tokenType ∈ {ACCESS, REFRESH}. Net: a stolen REFRESH token passes the platform-wide middleware on every Bearer-protected route — /cart/cart/add-item, /checkout/checkout/commit, /payment/intent/simulate, /order/order/cancel-mine, /identity/profile/me, /inventory/stock/adjust (admin-side via role claim), every customer-side endpoint. The blast radius is the entire customer surface for the longer-lived (14d) of the two tokens. R-L1 filed this as REV-IDENT-102 scoped to identity's Refresh handler and identity's /profile/me; the cross-component fact is that ALL 7 services share the broken middleware via the common module, so the fix has to land in common/middleware/auth.go to close it everywhere at once. Defense-in-depth proposed in ADR-002 (separate keypairs for ACCESS vs REFRESH) is also not implemented — both signers in identity use cfg.JWT.PrivateKeyPEM.
findings.recommendation: Tech-Lead: amend contracts.json#cross-cutting.auth.transport to mandate that common/middleware/auth.go MUST validate `claims.Extra['tokenType']` is 'access' (case-insensitive), rejecting otherwise with 401 AUTH_INVALID. Patch is two lines in middleware/auth.go after ValidateClaims: `if tt, _ := claim.Extra["tokenType"].(string); !strings.EqualFold(tt, "access") { abortUnauthorized(c); return }`. Symmetric inverse already needed in identity Refresh handler (REV-IDENT-102 covers that side). Reviewer regression test: refresh_token_on_cart_add_item_returns_AUTH_INVALID. Long-term hardening: add JWT_REFRESH_PRIVATE_KEY_PEM env var so AccessSigner and RefreshSigner use distinct ES256 keypairs (defense-in-depth per ADR-002 line allowing separate keys).

findings.locus: order/app/order/consumer.go:139-156 (stub onPaymentFailed/onPaymentExpired/onReservationExpired) ↔ payment outbox publisher ↔ inventory.sweeper events.reservation.expired
findings.description: Closure check on dry-run #1 REV-L2-004 (compound stub dead-end) is only HALF achieved. order.cancel-on-checkout-failure is a real handler now (handler_cancel_on_checkout_failure.go un-stubbed; ADR-007 land-true), so the synchronous saga compensation closes. BUT Order's three Kafka consumers for the asynchronous lifecycle remain TODO stubs at consumer.go:139, 146, 153 — every onPaymentFailed/onPaymentExpired/onReservationExpired logs 'TODO' and returns nil. System-level consequence: (a) when the customer simulates payment FAILED via /payment/intent/simulate, payment publishes events.payment.failed → Order's stub no-ops → orders.status stays PENDING_PAYMENT forever (state machine §9.2 says SYSTEM transitions to PAYMENT_FAILED never fire); (b) when the 60s payment expiry sweeper or the 30s inventory reservation sweeper transitions a stale intent/reservation to EXPIRED and publishes events.payment.expired or events.reservation.expired, Order's stubs no-op → orders.status stays PENDING_PAYMENT forever; (c) the customer's My Orders page reads PENDING_PAYMENT indefinitely on every failed/expired path; (d) stock returned to available_qty by inventory's sweeper is invisible in Order — admin can never tell why a reservation expired. The synchronous half (cancel-on-checkout-failure) only covers the rare race where Checkout itself fails between steps 6 and 8; the asynchronous half (payment failed/expired and reservation expired) is the COMMON case (every abandoned checkout, every customer who declined the simulate, every TTL hit) and the system has no way out. R-L1 filed REV-ORDER-003 only as a code-quality nit ('use ValidateTransition on payment.completed too'); the L2 view is that THREE of FOUR consumers are non-functional and the asynchronous lifecycle is dead. This is the same compound-stub-dead-end class as dry-run #1 REV-L2-004, just on the kafka consumer side instead of the synchronous compensation side. Fire again per the closure-check rule.
findings.recommendation: Tech-Lead: route to Order Dev for full implementation of the three consumer stubs to match the onPaymentCompleted state-driven shape (consumer.go:51-133): (i) BEGIN tx; (ii) consumed_events PK dedup; (iii) GetByIDForUpdate; (iv) `if err := ValidateTransition(order.Status, target, RoleSystem); err != nil { commit no-op }` — using the canonical ValidateTransition gate, NOT inline status comparison; (v) UpdateStatus + status_history insert; (vi) commit. Targets: payment.failed → PAYMENT_FAILED; payment.expired → PAYMENT_EXPIRED; reservation.expired → PAYMENT_EXPIRED (first-writer-wins via SELECT FOR UPDATE per ADR-009 PR-008). Reviewer regression: integration test 'payment.simulate FAILED → order.detail eventually reads PAYMENT_FAILED' and 'reservation TTL expires while order PENDING_PAYMENT → order.detail eventually reads PAYMENT_EXPIRED'. Without this, REV-L2-004 remains open and the platform cannot reach a terminal state on the failure paths.

findings.description: Cross-cutting.idempotency mandates that Idempotency-Key originates as an HTTP header at the customer's browser (CheckoutCommitButton.tsx:23-30 sets it) and flows verbatim through every hop to the leaf service. The chain is broken at every joint: (a) Frontend generates the key, sets it as 'Idempotency-Key' HTTP header on POST /api/checkout/commit, but no dedicated route handler exists at frontend/app/api/checkout/commit/route.ts — the request falls through to the [...path] catch-all (route.ts:57-77) which copies only Content-Type and Authorization, never the Idempotency-Key header (R-L1 REV-FRONTEND-WEB-001); (b) even if Frontend forwarded the header, Checkout's outbound clients DO NOT propagate it as an HTTP header — client_inventory.go:91-95 sends `idempotencyKey: orderId` as a JSON BODY field (Inventory accepts it via body — handler_reservation_create.go:46-47 reads req.IdempotencyKey, validates == req.OrderID), client_order.go sends it as JSON BODY field (Order's CreateFromCheckoutRequest binding:"required"), and client_payment.go sends NO idempotency-key at all — neither header nor body (R-L1 REV-PAYMENT-002 confirms Payment expects c.GetHeader('Idempotency-Key') and doesn't get one); (c) Payment intent.create therefore has zero replay protection in production — the contract defense-in-depth (ADR-007 idempotency_per_endpoint) is mute on the Payment hop. Net cross-component pattern: idempotency carriage uses three different mechanisms (header at frontend, body at inventory/order, missing at payment) for what the contract describes as ONE protocol. A retried Place-Order tap can therefore double-create payment intents under the same orderId; payment_callback_dedup table catches some but not all (the dedup is on (paymentIntentId, providerStatus), and a second create-intent generates a NEW paymentIntentId).
findings.recommendation: Tech-Lead: tighten contracts.json#cross-cutting.idempotency to specify that Idempotency-Key MUST be carried as the HTTP header 'Idempotency-Key' on every cross-service hop (no body-shadow allowed), and mandate the recipient service reads c.GetHeader('Idempotency-Key') NOT a body field. Then in execution: (i) Frontend Dev adds dedicated app/api/checkout/commit/route.ts (and /api/payment/simulate/route.ts) that withAuth-wraps and forwards the header (closes REV-FRONTEND-WEB-001); (ii) Checkout Dev adds an idempotencyKeyOption helper in client_helpers.go and calls it on every outbound to inventory.reservation.create, inventory.reservation.release, order.create-from-checkout, order.cancel-on-checkout-failure, payment.intent.create; (iii) Order/Inventory/Payment Devs read header instead of body (Inventory keeps the body field as a transient compat for one cycle, then drops). Reviewer regression: integration test asserts the same browser Idempotency-Key reaches the Payment recipient verbatim (instrument with a request-echo middleware in test).

findings.description: ADR-008 + connectivity.md authBoundaries (lines 159, 161, 167) state that inventory.reservation.create/release and payment.intent.create are X-Internal-Secret-only routes (called by Checkout, internal-only, with constant-time secret compare). Checkout's outbound clients carry only `bearerAuthOption(bearerToken)` — internalSecretOption is never invoked on these three call sites. Reviewer-L1 (CHK-QA-001) flagged this as a per-component code_mismatch but the cross-component manifestation is bigger: every Checkout commit currently 401s at Inventory (reservation/create and reservation/release routes are protected by inventory.InternalAuthMiddleware in inventory/router/router.go:87) and at Payment (payment/router/router.go:46-50 internalMW). With the dry-run #2 router protecting those routes correctly via X-Internal-Secret, Checkout cannot reach them at all — every commit fails at step 6 (inventory.reservation.create). The 'fix' the L1 reviewer described is a one-side patch (Checkout client adds the header). The cross-component view is that this is the worst-case interaction between three correct R-L1-level fixes: Inventory and Payment correctly protect their routes (INTERNAL_SHARED_SECRET unification + ConstantTimeCompare both work) but Checkout's clients were never updated to send the header — every checkout commit fails by construction. This is an end-to-end-broken commit path and ranks high (zero successful checkouts in the system) even though no individual L1 finding called it that.
findings.recommendation: Tech-Lead: this is per-component remediation but the L2 framing is a critical-path-zero-throughput dead end. Route to Checkout Dev (P0): in client_inventory.go and client_payment.go, accept an `internalSecret string` constructor argument like client_order.go:31 does; add internalSecretOption(c.internalSecret) to BulkReadStock, CreateReservation, ReleaseReservation, CreateIntent. Wire cfg.Internal.SharedSecret into the client constructors at router/deps.go. End-to-end smoke test: a happy-path commit must reach Inventory and Payment with both Bearer + X-Internal-Secret headers — assert via httptest middleware capture in an integration test.

findings.locus: order/main.go:60-79 (no outbox publisher goroutine) ↔ inventory consumer of events.order.cancelled ↔ payment consumer of events.order.cancelled
findings.description: Order's main.go starts the HTTP server and the Kafka subscriber but NEVER starts an outbox publisher goroutine. cancel-on-checkout-failure and (future) cancel-mine + admin update-status both write events.order.cancelled rows to outbox_events.published_at IS NULL, and PollUnpublished + MarkPublished are implemented (storage_outbox.go), but no goroutine drains them. ADR-004 outbox pattern is half-finished. System-level effect: every Order-side cancellation publishes nothing on Kafka → Inventory's state-driven consumer of events.order.cancelled (per ADR-009: RESERVED→RELEASED, COMMITTED→sold→available) NEVER FIRES → reservation rows accumulate in RESERVED until the 15-min TTL sweeper releases them (acceptable safety net for cancel-on-checkout-failure compensation, since Checkout also calls inventory.reservation.release synchronously) but for ANY future customer-cancel-mine or admin-cancel after PAID, the reservation/sold quantity is never restored to available because (i) Order publishes nothing, and (ii) the sweeper only handles RESERVED rows, not COMMITTED ones. R-L1 filed REV-ORDER-004 as a per-component MEDIUM; the cross-component view (Order ↔ Inventory ↔ Payment via the events.order.cancelled topic) is HIGH because one outbox publisher gap silently breaks the BA PR-006 MVP restock policy across two consumer services. Cancellation becomes inventory-toxic the moment cancel-mine and admin-cancel un-stub.
findings.recommendation: Tech-Lead: route to Order Dev. Add an OutboxPublisher goroutine in order/main.go alongside StartSubscriber: ~1s ticker, PollUnpublished(ctx, limit=100, ORDER BY id ASC), publish each row via common/kafka.Producer to ecom.order.events keyed by orderId, MarkPublished(id) on success, defer recover() with stack-trace log. Pattern to copy: catalog/main.go:138-191 startOutboxRelay (and harden against the catalog REV-CATALOG-002 panic-recovery gap at the same time). Reviewer regression: integration test asserts that cancel-on-checkout-failure publishes events.order.cancelled to Kafka within 2 seconds of commit, and that Inventory's consumer transitions the reservation state correctly.

findings.locus: frontend/lib/auth.ts:58-64 (clearAccessCookie/clearRefreshCookie) called from frontend/app/api/proxy/identity/auth/refresh/route.ts:74-75, frontend/app/api/proxy/identity/auth/logout/route.ts:22-23, frontend/lib/auth.ts:101-102 (withAuth AUTH_REVOKED branch)
findings.description: Build-cookie strings (auth.ts:51, 55) include `HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax;${cookieSecureFlag()}`; clear-cookie strings (auth.ts:59, 63) include only `HttpOnly` — they OMIT SameSite=Lax and (in production) Secure. The clearance string is invoked from THREE Set-Cookie sites: refresh route, logout route, and withAuth AUTH_REVOKED. Some browser cookie-store enforcement policies reject the overwriting Set-Cookie when the new attributes downgrade the original (Secure → no-Secure on HTTPS, SameSite=Lax → SameSite default), leaving the original session cookie alive after logout. R-L1 (REV-FRONTEND-WEB-002) filed this scoped to lib/auth.ts as a single high finding; the cross-component (or rather cross-Set-Cookie-site) parity view is that the asymmetry replays at every clearance site and the same broken code path executes from logout, refresh-revoked, and withAuth AUTH_REVOKED — three independent code paths inheriting one helper's bug. Cookie attribute parity (issuance vs clearance) is a cross-cutting hot zone called out explicitly in the L2 brief. Already-filed at L1, downgrading my severity here from HIGH to MEDIUM to avoid double-fire on per-component scope; including for the Tech-Lead awareness that this is the cross-cutting angle and the contracts.json#cross-cutting.cookies should mandate parity in spec, not just reviewer discipline.
findings.recommendation: Tech-Lead: amend contracts.json#cross-cutting.cookies (or security_posture.cookies.clearance in the TD) to mandate that clearance Set-Cookie strings MUST mirror the build strings on Path, HttpOnly, SameSite, and (in production) Secure attributes — only Max-Age=0 differs. Then auth.ts:59,63 changes to: ``return `access=; Path=/; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax;${cookieSecureFlag()} Max-Age=0`;`` (and refresh symmetric). Reviewer-L1 grep regression on the clearance helpers ensures every future clearance site inherits the fix.

findings.locus: all 4 internal-auth recipients (order/app/order/middleware_internal_auth.go, inventory/app/inventory/middleware_internal_auth.go, payment/router/router.go:64-80, checkout/router/router.go) — comma-separated rotation parsing missing; ADR-008 rotation_overlap clause unimplemented
findings.description: ADR-008 (LOCKED) §rotation_overlap explicitly says: 'the env var MAY accept a comma-separated value INTERNAL_SHARED_SECRET=new,old. Recipients try ConstantTimeCompare against each comma-segment; first match wins.' Of the four recipients, only Payment's R-L1 reviewer (REV-PAYMENT-003) flagged the missing comma-split — the other three middleware implementations also do a single ConstantTimeCompare against the whole string (order/middleware_internal_auth.go:35, inventory/middleware_internal_auth.go:38). The cross-component pattern is that all four services drifted the SAME way despite a shared ADR — the canonical helper backend/common/middleware/internal_auth.go that ADR-008 §shared_helper proposes does not exist (verified via search). Operational consequence: rotating INTERNAL_SHARED_SECRET requires a synchronized cold restart of all four services (impossible across a real environment in <30s) — the documented 5-minute overlap window cannot be exercised. Filed at MEDIUM (not HIGH) because (a) MVP rotation is rare, (b) Payment's R-L1 already flagged at the per-service level. The L2 framing: build the canonical common/middleware/internal_auth.go helper now and have all four services adopt it, instead of three more drifted per-service patches.
findings.recommendation: Tech-Lead: create backend/common/middleware/internal_auth.go implementing the ADR-008 contract — accept the secret as 'new,old' CSV, ConstantTimeCompare against each token, always run the full loop for timing constancy, log internal_auth_reject without logging the supplied or expected secret. Then four services migrate (one PR each) from per-service middleware to common/middleware. Reviewer regression: a unit test asserts that a request signed with the 'old' segment of a CSV secret authenticates successfully while the 'rotation' is in flight, and that segments do not leak via timing.

findings.description: Two services (Catalog and Cart) consume inventory.stock.bulk-read for the inStock filter and the Cart-read fan-out. Catalog's handler_product_list.go:181-190 declares the inStock filter, parses it into ProductListFilter, and DROPS it on the floor (no inventory client exists in app/catalog). Cart's service.go:340-347 calls inventory.stock.bulk-read inside a goroutine that swallows ALL errors (returns nil on any inventory failure, blocking the strict-error-policy errgroup cancellation). The cross-component pattern: TWO consumers of the same inventory.stock.bulk-read endpoint independently chose silent-degrade behavior contradicting the same TD strict-error-policy clause (mandates UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT 504 on any inventory unavailability). R-L1 filed each side separately (REV-CATALOG-001 and REV-CART-001) but the L2 view is the systemic pattern: cross-cutting.fan_out_spec.error_policy is interpreted differently by Catalog and Cart and probably by future consumers (Order admin search, Checkout step 4b — checkout DOES return UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT correctly, the only one of three callers to honor the contract). Without a Tech-Lead-provided shared client wrapper enforcing the strict-error-policy at the call site, every new consumer will redo the wrong choice. Maintainability tag because the security and bug consequences are already filed at L1 — the L2 contribution is the systemic-pattern detection.
findings.recommendation: Tech-Lead: add backend/common/clients/inventory_stock.go a thin shared wrapper that returns sentinel ErrUpstreamTimeout / ErrInsufficientStock and never silently swallows; cross-cutting.fan_out_spec.error_policy mandates use of this wrapper (ban direct net/http calls to /inventory/stock/bulk-read in any service except Inventory itself). Catalog wires it (closes REV-CATALOG-001 systemically), Cart wires it (closes REV-CART-001 systemically), Checkout already does the right thing at the call site so the migration is a code-cleanup. Reviewer regression: cross-service grep that no service other than common/clients constructs `c.baseURL + "/api/v1/inventory/stock/bulk-read"`.

findings.locus: outbox publisher pattern divergence — catalog/main.go:83 (bare `go startOutboxRelay`, no panic-recovery) vs payment (per ADR-006 with dedup) vs order (NOT WIRED — REV-L2-106)
findings.description: Three of four publisher-side services (Catalog, Payment, Order) write to outbox_events tables with the same intended pattern (POLL → SEND → MARK PUBLISHED on a ~1s ticker). Each implementation drifted: Catalog has the goroutine but no defer/recover (REV-CATALOG-002, REV-CATALOG-003: FOR UPDATE locks released between Fetch and MarkPublished); Order has no goroutine at all (REV-L2-106 above); Payment's pattern is documented but not yet checked at L1 since their callback dedup is a different concern. ADR-004 outbox pattern was supposed to land via a shared pattern; instead it landed thrice independently. Advisory only — system-level fixes are in REV-L2-106 (Order) and REV-CATALOG-002/003 (Catalog L1); the cross-component framing is that a common/outbox/relay.go shared helper would have prevented all three drifts.
findings.recommendation: Tech-Lead: add to the v3 backlog (NOT MVP) — common/outbox/relay.go shared helper exposing StartRelay(ctx, db, producer, opts) with mandatory defer/recover, in-tx FOR UPDATE + MarkPublished, batch=100, jitter on the ticker. ADR-004 amendment to require it. Not a block-merge gate; a maintainability nudge.
